whyItMatters: Beanstalk configuration reads are often the first step in credential or trust-path discovery. Even when legitimate, they are valuable reconnaissance telemetry.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may inspect Beanstalk configuration settings to identify secrets, environment variables, role references, or other useful pivot material.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is attractive because it uses a read-only administrative API that may appear benign in environments with limited Beanstalk monitoring.
threatContext.whyItMatters: This baseline event feeds stronger detections about unauthorized readers, burst enumeration, and recon-to-action sequences.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, defenders may overlook the earliest stage of Beanstalk-derived credential theft.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for Elastic Beanstalk
loggingRequirements: CloudTrail must ingest Elastic Beanstalk management events.
The platform should retain application and environment context.
Follow-on IAM, STS, and secrets events should be available for downstream correlation.
limitations: The API does not by itself prove that secrets were exposed or abused.
Legitimate application and platform administrators may use it regularly.
A single read is lower confidence without actor or follow-on context.

enrichment.description: Classify the Beanstalk environment by privilege exposure and business criticality.
Determine whether the actor normally administers or inspects Beanstalk configuration.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Turns baseline visibility into stronger actor-based detections.

enrichment.description: Assess whether the environment is known to carry secrets or secret references in config.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Raises urgency when the read likely exposes useful material.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This should remain a broad visibility rule for successful `DescribeConfigurationSettings` events. It establishes the Beanstalk recon baseline that stronger actor, burst, and recon-to-action detections depend on.
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Keep this baseline broad. 2. Resolve environment sensitivity and actor context for triage. 3. Correlate with later IAM, STS, or secrets access for higher-confidence detections.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire on every successful DescribeConfigurationSettings event for visibility.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Medium as a baseline visibility rule, low-medium with environment and actor context

deployment.scheduling: Real-time is useful for chaining into follow-on credential-theft detections.
considerations: This is the feeder rule for the Beanstalk credential-theft family.
Environment sensitivity and actor context are the main enrichments.
